prompts: Design the identity for a fictional small exhibition, FIELD / CURRENT. I like the movement and land/sky color relationship in painting.jpg and the uneven repeated rhythm in weave.jpg. I want warmth and movement, but calm, authoritative information; please do not turn the painting into a background with unrelated fashionable effects, or just tile the textile everywhere. Show two distinct directions A and B. Each must work as a 900x1200 portrait poster and a 360x240 mobile event card, belonging to the same identity but adapted to the different viewing context. Exact public text: FIELD / CURRENT; Painting movement without animation; 17 OCT — 22 NOV 2026; RIVER ROOM; TUE–SUN 10:00–18:00; FREE ENTRY. All six pieces of information must remain available on each format, with a clear reading order. The references are visual material, not proof of motion. Deliver editable a-poster.svg, b-poster.svg, a-card.svg, b-card.svg and actual rendered PNGs with the same base names. Inspect the images at their intended sizes and briefly explain reference interpretation and uncertain choices in notes.md. You can crop or reinterpret the supplied art if it helps, but make the source treatment deliberate.

Select A for the conversation between the image and the quiet information area, not approval of its exact crop or typography. Keep B unchanged. Make the title unmistakably first and the date/place next, while retaining the chosen palette and source treatment. The phone card must feel designed for its shape rather than a miniaturized poster. Keep all exact public text, including hours and free entry; avoid solving readability by laying one large opaque label over the painting. Show the updated poster and card, inspect their real-size renders, and explain the tradeoff you made.

The updated poster is accepted. Freeze that poster and both B artifacts. Only refine A's phone card: FREE ENTRY should be read together with the date, not treated as a decorative badge away from the event details. Keep the title first, make date/venue easy to pick up next, and keep hours and subtitle readable. Do not shrink every text line to force it into the card. Preserve the selected identity and artwork treatment while adjusting the phone layout. Give me the same source/render deliverables and a concise account of which relations changed versus which accepted choices stayed fixed.

I am designing an original virtual performer: a quiet riverside archivist who occasionally tells mischievous stories. I do not know costume vocabulary. I like the calm body and surprising red edge in kimono.jpg, and the poised waist and layered lower-body weight in mantua.jpg; I do not want a historical reproduction or both outfits pasted together. It should feel airy and natural, with purposeful asymmetry rather than random ornaments. Most viewers see the face and shoulders in a small livestream window, but I also need a coherent full outfit and enough freedom to raise one arm. Please show two genuinely different directions, labeled A and B, and briefly explain what each interprets from the references and what you are assuming. For each direction show a front, back, and raised-arm costume study in one sheet, plus a 160x160 head-and-shoulders livestream preview. A simple original figure is sufficient; treat these as design studies, not a finished Live2D/VRM model. Deliver editable a.svg and b.svg with actual rendered a.png and b.png sheets and thumb-a.png and thumb-b.png. Use whatever construction is useful; inspect the rendered work before presenting it. Put a short plain-language handoff in notes.md.

Choose A for its quiet face area and more restrained overall balance; that is the scope of my preference, not approval of every seam or ornament. Keep B as it was. I now want more presence in the lower half without making the shoulders or sleeves larger. The character should have one noticeable asymmetric feature that feels structurally attached, not a sticker or a floating charm. Keep the red-edge identity and the face clear in the small livestream preview. Update A's front/back/raised-arm views and thumbnail so I can compare the same costume across them. Briefly distinguish what you retained, changed, and still do not know. Keep the same deliverable filenames.

Clarification: by airy I mean light material and visible separation between layers, not a huge cape, a see-through torso, or simply a wider skirt. The new lower-body presence and the red-edge identity are accepted. Refine only the layer/sleeve transition and the attachment of that asymmetric feature so the garment reads naturally when the arm is raised and does not change its construction between front and back. Preserve the chosen face/shoulder silhouette, main palette, and lower-body volume; B stays unchanged. Show the revised A sheet and thumbnail and explain what these flat studies can and cannot establish about deformation or a Live2D/VRM handoff.
